Rashi on Kiddushin 61b:10:1.hebrew: בשלמא לר' מאיר - דאמר מכללא לא שמעי', היינו דכתיב: "אז תנקה מאלתי". לפי שהשביעו: "אם לא אל בית אבי תלך" — תחול עליך שבועה, ומכללא לא שמעינן דאם תלך לא תחול:
Rashi on Kiddushin 61b:10:1.english: Granted, according to Rabbi Meir - For he says [that] we do not infer from an implication; this is [why] it is written: “Then you shall be clear from my oath.” For since he adjured him, “If you do not go to my father’s house,” [meaning that] the oath shall take effect upon you, and from the implication we would not infer that if you do go, it will not take effect.

Rashi on Kiddushin 61b:10:2.hebrew: למה לי - לפרושי "אם תלך תנקה"? אלא דאי לא כפליה לא הוה מבטל תנאה לשבועה, דאפי' ילך תחול עליו אם יקח לו אשה מבנות כנען:
Rashi on Kiddushin 61b:10:2.english: Why do I need [it] - [Is it needed] to specify: "If you go, you will be clear"? [Could it be] that if he had not doubled it, the condition would not have nullified the oath, so that even if he goes, [the oath] would take effect upon him if he takes a wife from the daughters of Canaan?!

Rashi on Kiddushin 61b:11:1.english: Where it is satisfactory to her - To the woman.

Rashi on Kiddushin 61b:11:2.english: And it is not satisfactory to them - To [her] relatives.

Rashi on Kiddushin 61b:12:1.hebrew: נייתי - להכי נכתב האי, למיתלי נמי בקרובים: ״ואם לא יתנו לך״ — קרובים — ״והיית נקי״:
Rashi on Kiddushin 61b:12:1.english: He should bring [her] - For this [reason] this was written, to make [it] dependent on the relatives as well: “And if they do not give [her] to you” — [meaning the] relatives — “then you shall be clear.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 61b:13:1.hebrew: למה לי - ״ואם בחקותי תמאסו״? נשמע מכלל ברכה קללה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 61b:13:1.english: Why do I [need it] - [Why do I need] “And if you shall reject My statutes”? Let a curse be inferred from the implication of the blessing.

Rashi on Kiddushin 61b:15:1.hebrew: מקמי דנימא ליה ר' מאיר - "אם כן נכתוב 'ונאחזו'". והוה סבר ר' חנינא דכולא מילתא דריש רבי מאיר לתנאי כפול; הלכך אמר ליה, שאלמלא כן, שכפל דבריו, יש משמע שאף בארץ כנען לא יטלו, וכ"ש במקום החביב להם, דמכלל הן היינו שומעין לאו: "ואם לא יעברו לא תתנו להם את ארץ גלעד", וממילא דבארץ כנען לא שקלי, דהא לא אזלי למכבשה. וברייתא דקתני דלא אהני כפילה אלא לארץ כנען — אמר רבי חנינא בתר דאמר ליה ר' מאיר: "נכתוב קרא 'ונאחזו', למ"ל 'בארץ כנען'?", אמר ליה ר' חנינא: ליטול חלק בארץ כנען אהני, דאי לא כתביה הוה אמינא: "ונאחזו בתוככם" — בארץ גלעד:
Rashi on Kiddushin 61b:15:1.english: Before Rabbi Meir said to him - [Namely,] "If so, let [the verse] write: 'And they shall receive a possession' [without adding 'in the land of Canaan']." And Rabbi Ḥanina had thought that Rabbi Meir derived the entire requirement of a compound condition from the [entire] matter. Therefore, he said to him [in the Mishnah] that were it not so, that [Moses] doubled his words, it would imply that even in the land of Canaan they would not take [a portion], and all the more so in the place that was dear to them [the land of Gilead]; for from the positive we would infer the negative: "And if they do not cross over, do not give them the land of Gilead," and consequently they would not take [a portion] in the land of Canaan [either], as they did not go to conquer it. And the baraita, which teaches that the doubling was only effective for [granting an inheritance in] the land of Canaan, Rabbi Ḥanina stated after Rabbi Meir said to him: "Let the verse write: 'And they shall receive a possession'; why do I need 'in the land of Canaan'?" Rabbi Ḥanina said to him: It was effective [to teach that they] take a portion in the land of Canaan, for had [the verse] not written it, I would have said: "'And they shall receive a possession among you' [means] in the land of Gilead."

Rashi on Kiddushin 61b:1:1.hebrew: למה לי - בארץ כנען, דמשמע מיעוטא, למעוטי שלא יטלו בארץ גלעד כנגד חלקם שבארץ כנען? (הרי משמע נמי מונאחזו בתוככם שלא יטלו בארץ גלעד כנגד חלקם שבארץ ישראל, אלא קרא יתירא הוא למדרש ביה תנאי כפול). ש"מ: הוצרך לכפול ולומר: ״אם לא יעברו לא יהא בדברי כלום״; ואי לא כפלו — היתה מתנתו קיימת, דמכלל הן לא נשמע לאו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 61b:1:1.english: Why do I [need it] - [Why do I need] “in the land of Canaan”, which implies an exclusion, to exclude [them] so that they should not receive [land] in the land of Gilead corresponding to their portion that is in the land of Canaan? (Behold, it is also implied by “and they shall receive a possession among you” that they should not receive [land] in the land of Gilead corresponding to their portion that is in the Land of Israel; rather, it is a superfluous verse to expound from it [the requirement of] a compound condition.) Conclude from it: He was required to double [the condition] and say, “If they will not pass over, there shall be nothing to my words”; for had he not doubled it, his gift would have remained valid, because from an affirmative [statement], a negative is not inferred.

Rashi on Kiddushin 61b:2:1.hebrew: ורבי חנינא - אמר לך: לעולם לא בא לכפול, אלא לפרש שאפי' לא יעברו לא יפסידו נחלתם מכל ארץ ישראל. ואם כתב "ונאחזו בתוככם" ותו לא, ה"א: ואם לא יעברו יטלו כפי המגיעם בארץ הגלעד שנאחזתם בה כבר והם סייעו אתכם לכבשה, אבל בארץ כנען כלל לא — לא בתוכה יטלו, ולא בארץ גלעד כנגדה. להכי כתב "בארץ כנען", שאף בארץ כנען יטלו, אע"פ שלא סייעו לכובשה. אבל למעוטי שלא יטלו ארץ הגלעד כנגדה לא איצטריך, דמכלל הן הוה שמעינן לאו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 61b:2:1.english: And Rabbi Ḥanina - [could] say to you: In truth, [the verse] did not come to double [the condition], but to clarify that even if they do not cross over, they will not forfeit their inheritance from the entire Land of Israel. For if it had written, “they shall have possessions among you,” and nothing more, I would have said: If they do not cross over, they will receive according to what is due to them in the land of Gilead, in which you have already taken possession and which they helped you conquer; but in the land of Canaan, not at all — neither will they receive [a portion] within it, nor in the land of Gilead in place of it. Therefore, it wrote “in the land of Canaan,” [to teach] that they shall receive [a portion] even in the land of Canaan, even though they did not assist in conquering it. But to exclude [them] so that they would not receive the land of Gilead in place of it was not necessary [to state], for from the affirmative [statement], we would infer the negative.

Rashi on Kiddushin 61b:2:2.hebrew: כל היכא דאית לכו משמע - ועל כרחך, לא כתב "בארץ כנען" אלא למעוטי ארץ גלעד — שלא יטלוה כולה על פי מתנתו שאמר להם: "ונתתם להם" — וללמדינו דמכלל הן לא הוה שמעינן לאו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 61b:2:2.english: [It] means anywhere that you have - And perforce, [the verse] wrote “in the land of Canaan” only to exclude the land of Gilead — so that they would not take all of it in accordance with his gift, as he said to them: “You shall give them [the land of Gilead]” — and to teach us that from a positive [statement] we would not infer the negative.

Rashi on Kiddushin 61b:3:1.english: A parable - [Illustrating the condition] of Moses.

Rashi on Kiddushin 61b:3:2.hebrew: למה הדבר דומה כו' - כך: שאר השבטים יטלו ארץ כנען, ושני שבטים אלו יעברו את הירדן למלחמה — דהיינו דומיא דיתן להם מאתים זוז — ויטלו ארץ הגלעד. ואם לא יעברו, לא יפסידו חלקם בארץ כנען — דהיינו שאר נכסים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 61b:3:2.english: To what is this matter comparable, etc. - So [too]: The other tribes will receive the land of Canaan, and these two tribes will cross the Jordan for war — which is analogous to "he shall give them two hundred dinars" — and [thereby] receive the land of Gilead. And if they do not cross over, they will not forfeit their portion in the land of Canaan — which is [analogous to] "the rest of the property."

Rashi on Kiddushin 61b:4:1.hebrew: מי גרם לו ליטול עם אחיו בשאר נכסים כפילו גרמא לו - דאם לא כפל, הייתי שומע: דאם לא יתן — יטול באותו שדה כפי חלק המגיעו בו, אבל בשתי שדות שהקציתים לאחיו לא יטול כלום, וכל שכן שלא יטול באותו שדה כנגד שאר נכסים. אף בני גד ובני ראובן — כפילת הדברים גרמא להם ליטול חלקם בארץ כנען, שאם לא כפל הייתי אומר: לא יטלו בה כלום, אלא בארץ גלעד מה שמגיעם בה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 61b:4:1.english: What caused him to take with his brothers in the rest of the property? His doubling caused it - For had he not doubled [the condition], I would have understood that if he does not give [the money], he would take in that field according to the portion that is due to him in it, but in the two fields that [the father] designated for his brothers, he would not take anything, and all the more so he would not take in that field [a portion] corresponding to the rest of the property. So too, [regarding] the children of Gad and the children of Reuben, the doubling of the statement caused them to take their portion in the Land of Canaan; for had he not doubled [it], I would have said: They shall not take anything in it, but rather in the land of Gilead [only] that which is due to them in it.

Rashi on Kiddushin 61b:5:1.hebrew: התם - מתני' קתני שאם לא כפל לא היו נוטלין כלום, לא כאן ולא כאן, דקאמר: שאף בארץ כנען, שאיננה חביבה להם, לא יטלו. מדקתני ״שאף״, משמע דכל שכן בארץ גלעד שבחרו בה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 61b:5:1.english: There - The Mishnah teaches that if he had not doubled [the condition], they would not take anything, neither here nor there, for it says that even in the land of Canaan, which was not dear to them, they would not take [a portion]. From the fact that it teaches “that even,” it implies that all the more so in the land of Gilead, which they chose.

Rashi on Kiddushin 61b:5:2.hebrew: ה"ג: אלמא כפילא לארץ גלעד נמי אהני, והכא קתני מי גרם לו כו' - אלמא לא אהני אלא אארץ כנען, דבלאו כפילה נמי הוו שקלי מה שמגיעם בארץ גלעד:
Rashi on Kiddushin 61b:5:2.english: This is the reading: “Consequently, the double condition was effective for the land of Gilead as well; and here it teaches: What caused him, etc.?” - It follows that it was effective only regarding the land of Canaan, for even without the double condition, they would have taken what was due to them in the land of Gilead.

Rashi on Kiddushin 61b:7:1.hebrew: לא קשיא - מתני' דקתני ״שאף״, דמשמע דכל שכן בארץ גלעד:
Rashi on Kiddushin 61b:7:1.english: This is not difficult - [This refers to] the Mishnah, which teaches "that even," which implies that all the more so [they would not inherit] in the land of Gilead.

Rashi on Kiddushin 61b:7:2.hebrew: מקמי דנימא ליה ר' מאיר - אם כן, נכתוב "ונאחזו". והוה סבר ר' חנינא דכולא מילתא דריש רבי מאיר לתנאי כפול. הלכך, אמר ליה: שאלמלא כן, שכפל דבריו, יש משמע שאף בארץ כנען לא יטלו, וכ"ש במקום החביב להם, דמכלל הן היינו שומעין לאו — "ואם לא יעברו לא תתנו להם את ארץ גלעד" — וממילא דבארץ כנען לא שקלי, דהא לא אזלי למכבשה. וברייתא, דקתני דלא אהני כפילה אלא לארץ כנען, אמר רבי חנינא בתר דאמר ליה ר' מאיר: נכתוב קרא "ונאחזו", למ"ל "בארץ כנען"? אמר ליה ר' חנינא: ליטול חלק בארץ כנען אהני, דאי לא כתביה, הוה אמינא: "ונאחזו בתוככם" — בארץ גלעד:
Rashi on Kiddushin 61b:7:2.english: Before Rabbi Meir said to him - [That is,] "If so, let [the verse] write: 'And they shall receive a possession' [without specifying 'in the land of Canaan']." And Rabbi Ḥanina [initially] thought that Rabbi Meir expounds the entire clause as [teaching the requirement of] a compound condition. Therefore, [Rabbi Ḥanina] said to him [in the Mishnah]: Were it not so, that [Moshe] doubled his words, it would imply that even in the land of Canaan they would not take [a portion], and all the more so in the place that is dear to them [the land of Gilead] — for from the affirmative we would have deduced the negative: "And if they do not pass over, you shall not give them the land of Gilead," and as a matter of course they would not take [a portion] in the land of Canaan either, since they did not go to conquer it. And the *baraita*, which teaches that the doubling [of the condition] was effective only for the land of Canaan, was stated by Rabbi Ḥanina after Rabbi Meir said to him: "Let Scripture write: 'And they shall receive a possession'; why do I need 'in the land of Canaan'?" Rabbi Ḥanina said to him: It was effective [to teach that they are] to take a portion in the land of Canaan; for had [Scripture] not written it, I would have said: "And they shall receive a possession among you" [means] in the land of Gilead.

Rashi on Kiddushin 61b:9:1.english: [Shall it not be] lifted up - A portion of reward.

Rashi on Kiddushin 61b:9:2.hebrew: ואם לא תיטיב לפתח - פורענות מוכנת לבא. אלמא, כפילה בעינן; ואם לא כפליה — מכי אמר ״אם תיטיב שאת״, הוה שמעי' דאפי' אם לא תיטיב נמי שאת, דתנאי שלא כפלו אינו מבטל מתנה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 61b:9:2.english: “And if you do not do well, at the door” - Retribution is ready to come. Thus, [we see that] we require a doubled [condition]; and had He not doubled it, once He said: “If you do well, [there is] reward,” we would have understood that even if you do not do well, [there is] also reward, for a condition that was not doubled does not void a gift.

Rashi on Kiddushin 61b:9:3.english: Why do I need [this] - [From] "If you do well," [the opposite] is understood by implication.

Rashi on Kiddushin 61b:9:4.hebrew: ס"ד כו' - כלומר, מכללא לא הוה נפקא לן אלא ביטול מתנה: הא אם לא תיטיב לא תשא שכר, ופורענותא נמי לא תשקול. להכי איצטריך כפילה — דינא דפורענותא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 61b:9:4.english: It might enter your mind, etc. - That is to say, from the implication [alone], all that would be derived for us is the cancellation of the gift: namely, if you do not do well, you will not receive a reward, but neither would you receive punishment. For this [reason], the doubling was necessary: [to teach] the judgment of punishment.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 61b:10:1.hebrew: בשלמא לרבי מאיר היינו דכתיב אז תנקה מאלתי אלא לר' חנינא למה לי - תימה: מה ענין זה אצל מחלוקת? והלא לא היה תנאי, אלא בפירוש אמר שישבע לו שיקח אשה לבנו ממשפחתו! ואם לא פירש הקרא "תנקה מאלתי אם לא יתנו לך", הייתי אומר שהיה עובר שבועה בין יתנו ובין לא יתנו, אם לא היה מביא אשה! ומה שפירש הקונטרס — קשה להבין; שהרי משמע מתוך פי' שאם הלך אליעזר למשפחת אברהם והם לא ירצו ליתן לו, שיהא מותר בבנות כנען, וזה אינו [דלפי זה סד"א דר"ח ב"ג איירי בע"א ממה שאמר ר"מ]. לכן פר"י: בשלמא לר' מאיר, דלית ליה "מכלל הן אתה שומע לאו", אע"פ שסברא הוא כשאדם מתנה עם חבירו "אם תעשה זה אתן לך זה, ואם לא תעשה לא אתן לך", כמו כן כאן, אע"פ שהוא סברא שלא השביעו אלא על מנת שיתנו, הוצרך לפרש "אם לא יתנו תהיה נקי"; אבל לר' חנינא, דאזיל בתר סברא לפי דעת בעלי התנאים, למה פירש "אם לא יתנו לך"? פשיטא, אם לא ירצו ליתן דיהיה נקי! ולמה"ר יצחק נראה ששתי שבועות השביעו: אחת שיקח אשה לבנו ממשפחתו, ושבועה אחרת שאם לא יתנו לא תקח אשה מבנות כנען; ודייק מדכתיב "ונקית משבועתי זאת", משמע שיש שבועה אחרת:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 61b:10:1.english: Granted, according to Rabbi Meir, this is what is written: "Then you shall be clear from my oath," but according to Rabbi Ḥanina, why do I need this? - It is astonishing: What relevance does this have to the dispute [between Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Ḥanina ben Gamliel]? Surely there was no condition here, but rather he explicitly told him to swear to him that he would take a wife for his son from his family! And had Scripture not specified: "You shall be clear from my oath... if they will not give [her] to you," I would have said that he would transgress the oath whether they give [her] or whether they do not give [her], if he did not bring a wife! And what Rashi explained is difficult to understand, for it implies from his explanation that if Eliezer went to Abraham's family and they did not want to give him [a wife], he would be permitted [to take a wife from] the daughters of Canaan — and this is not so! [For according to this, the initial assumption of Rabbi Ḥanina ben Gamliel would be dealing with a different scenario from what Rabbi Meir said]. Therefore, Rabbeinu Yitzḥak explained: Granted according to Rabbi Meir, who does not hold that from a positive statement you infer the negative, even though it is logical when a person stipulates with his fellow, "If you do this I will give you this, and if you do not do [this] I will not give you [this]" — so too here, even though it is logical that he adjured him only on condition that they agree to give [her], it was necessary to specify: "If they do not give [her], you shall be clear." But according to Rabbi Ḥanina [ben Gamliel], who follows logic according to the intent of the parties to the stipulation, why did [the verse] specify: "If they will not give [her] to you"? It is obvious that if they do not want to give [her], he would be clear! And to our master Rabbi Isaac, it appears that he adjured him with two oaths: one that he must take a wife for his son from his family, and another oath that [even] if they do not give [her], you shall not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan. And he deduced this from that which is written: "Then you shall be clear from this oath of mine" (Genesis 24:8), which implies that there is another oath [from which he is not cleared].

Tosafot on Kiddushin 61b:15:1.hebrew: אי לא כתב ארץ כנען ה"א בתוככם בארץ גלעד - פי' בקונט': דאם לא יעברו, יטלו חלקם כפי המגיעם בארץ גלעד, שנאחזו בה כבר והם סייעו [אתכם] לכבשה; אבל בארץ כנען — כלל וכלל לא, שהרי לא סייעו לכבשה. קא משמע לן דאעפ"כ יטלו. וקשה: וכי איזו סברא היא שישבו בבתיהם וירשו עם אחיהם שיצאו למלחמה?! [ועוד, דאינו דומה למשל דמייתי.] לכך נראה לר"י לפרש, דפשטיה דקרא הכי: אם יעברו חלוצים בראשי הצבא להיות ראשונים במלחמה — בשכר טובה זו שיעשו עם אחיהם תנתן להם ארץ הגלעד; ואם לא יתאמצו יותר מאחיהם — "ונאחזו". והכי נפרש: דאי לא כתב "בארץ כנען", ה"א שאם לא יעברו חלוצים בראש המלחמה, ולא יסייעו בכיבוש הארץ אלא כשאר שבטים — כלל וכלל לא יטלו מארץ כנען; קמשמע לן דאף על פי כן יטלו. וקשה: דהיכי תיסק אדעתיה שלא יטלו כלל בארץ כנען, כיון שסייעו בכיבוש כמו אחרים?! וי"ל: דסד"א, כיון שהוקצה ארץ כנען לשאר שבטים — שהרי מאותה שעה ששאלו בני גד ובני ראובן ארץ גלעד, נעשו כמו שסלקו עצמן מלחלוק בארץ כנען, ונימא שאם לא יקיימו תנאם לא יהיה להם חלק בה; קא משמע לן "בארץ כנען", לומר שיטלו חלקם כשאר שבטים, כאן וכאן. ואם תאמר: לכתוב קרא "בארץ כנען" בלבד, ולא נכתוב "ונאחזו בתוככם", וממילא ידענו, כיון שנוטלים חלקם בארץ שהוקצה לשאר שבטים, כ"ש שיטלו חלקם בארץ גלעד שלא הוקצה לשאר שבטים?! וי"ל: דאדרבה, ה"א בארץ כנען שלא נתייפה כחם — דין הוא שיטלו; אבל בארץ גלעד שנתייפה כחם בה — יקנסו ממנה, ולא יקחו בה כלל. לכך נכתבו שניהם. "בשלמא לרבי מאיר היינו דכתיב: 'אז תנקה מאלתי', אלא לר' חנינא למה לי?" — תימה: מה ענין זה אצל מחלוקת? והלא לא היה תנאי, אלא בפירוש אמר שישבע לו שיקח אשה לבנו ממשפחתו! ואם לא פירש הקרא "תנקה מאלתי... אם לא יתנו לך", הייתי אומר שהיה עובר שבועה בין יתנו ובין לא יתנו אם לא היה מביא אשה! ומה שפירש הקונטרס — קשה להבין; שהרי משמע מתוך פי' שאם הלך אליעזר למשפחת אברהם והם לא ירצו ליתן לו, שיהא מותר בבנות כנען — וזה אינו! [דלפי זה, סד"א דר"ח ב"ג איירי בע"א ממה שאמר ר"מ.] לכן פר"י: בשלמא לר' מאיר דלית ליה מכלל הן אתה שומע לאו, אע"פ שסברא הוא כשאדם מתנה עם חבירו "אם תעשה זה אתן לך זה, ואם לא תעשה לא אתן לך" — כמו כן כאן, אע"פ שהוא סברא שלא השביעו אלא על מנת שיתנו, הוצרך לפרש "אם לא יתנו תהיה נקי". אבל לר' חנינא דאזיל בתר סברא לפי דעת בעלי התנאים, למה פירש "אם לא יתנו לך"? פשיטא, אם לא ירצו ליתן — דיהיה נקי! ולמה"ר יצחק נראה: ששתי שבועות השביעו: אחת — שיקח אשה לבנו ממשפחתו; ושבועה אחרת — שאם לא יתנו, לא תקח אשה מבנות כנען. ודייק מדכתיב "ונקית משבועתי זאת" — משמע שיש שבועה אחרת:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 61b:15:1.english: Had it not written “the land of Canaan,” I would have said: “among you” [means] in the land of Gilead — The Kunteres explained that if they do not cross over, they will take their portion according to what is due to them in the land of Gilead, in which they had already settled and which they helped [you] to conquer; but in the land of Canaan, not at all, as they did not help conquer it. [The verse therefore] teaches us that nevertheless they will take [a portion in Canaan]. And this is difficult: For what logic is there that they should sit in their homes and inherit with their brethren who went out to war?! [And furthermore, it does not resemble the parable that was brought.] Therefore, it appears to the Ri to explain that the plain meaning of the verse is as follows: If they cross over as the vanguard at the head of the army, to be first in battle, in reward for this favor that they will do for their brethren, the land of Gilead will be given to them; and if they will not exert themselves more than their brethren, then “they shall receive a possession.” And this is how we explain [the Gemara]: Had it not written “in the land of Canaan,” I would have said that if they do not cross over as the vanguard at the head of the battle, and do not assist in the conquest of the Land other than like the rest of the tribes, they will not take anything from the land of Canaan at all. [The verse therefore] teaches us that nevertheless they will take [their portion]. And this is difficult: For how could it enter your mind that they would not take at all in the land of Canaan, given that they assisted in the conquest like the others?! And it can be answered: For it might enter your mind to say that since the land of Canaan was designated for the rest of the tribes — as from that moment when the children of Gad and the children of Reuben asked for the land of Gilead, it was as though they removed themselves from dividing the land of Canaan — and [so] we would say that if they do not fulfill their condition, they will have no share in it. [The verse therefore] teaches us “in the land of Canaan,” to say that they will take their portion like the rest of the tribes, here and here [i.e., both in Canaan and in Gilead]. And if you say: Let the verse write “in the land of Canaan” alone, and let it not write “and they shall receive a possession among you,” and we would automatically know that since they take their portion in the land that was designated for the rest of the tribes, all the more so they should take their portion in the land of Gilead, which was not designated for the rest of the tribes! And it can be answered: That on the contrary, I would have said that in the land of Canaan, where their standing was not enhanced, it is right that they should take [a portion]; but in the land of Gilead, where their standing was enhanced, they should be penalized regarding it and should not take anything in it at all. Therefore, both were written. [Regarding the Gemara's statement:] Granted according to Rabbi Meir, that is what is written: “Then you shall be clear from my oath” (Genesis 24:41); but according to Rabbi Ḥanina, why do I [need this]? — It is astonishing: What relevance does this have to their dispute? For was there not no condition here, but rather he explicitly said that he should swear to him that he would take a wife for his son from his family? And had the verse not specified “you shall be clear from my oath…if they will not give her to you,” I would have said that he would violate the oath whether they give or whether they do not give, if he did not bring a wife! And that which the Kunteres explained is difficult to understand: For it implies from his explanation that if Eliezer went to Abraham’s family and they did not wish to give him [a wife], he would be permitted [to take a wife from] the daughters of Canaan — and that is not so! [For according to this, it would enter your mind to say that Rabbi Ḥanina ben Gamliel is dealing with a different matter than what Rabbi Meir said.] Therefore, the Ri explained: Granted according to Rabbi Meir, who does not hold that from a positive statement you infer the negative even though it is logical — [just as] when a person stipulates with his fellow: “If you do this, I will give you this, and if you do not do it, I will not give you” — so too here, even though it is logical that he only adjured him on the condition that they would agree to give, he needed to specify: “If they will not give, you shall be clear.” But according to Rabbi Ḥanina, who follows logic according to the intention of the parties to the stipulation, why did he specify “if they will not give you”? It is obvious: if they do not wish to give, he should be clear! And to our teacher, Rabbi Isaac, it appears that he administered two oaths to him: One, that he should take a wife for his son from his family; and another oath, that even if they will not give, he shall not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan. And he deduces this from that which is written: “Then you shall be clear from this my oath” (Genesis 24:8), which implies that there is another oath [from which he is not released]:

Tosafot on Kiddushin 61b:2:1.hebrew: אי לא כתב ארץ כנען ה"א בתוככם בארץ גלעד - פי' בקונט': דאם לא יעברו, יטלו חלקם כפי המגיעם בארץ גלעד שנאחזו בה כבר, והם סייעו [אתכם] לכבשה; אבל בארץ כנען — כלל וכלל לא, שהרי לא סייעו לכבשה. קא משמע לן, דאעפ"כ יטלו. וקשה: וכי איזו סברא היא שישבו בבתיהם וירשו עם אחיהם שיצאו למלחמה?! [ועוד, דאינו דומה למשל דמייתי.] לכך נראה לר"י לפרש, דפשטיה דקרא הכי: אם יעברו חלוצים בראשי הצבא להיות ראשונים במלחמה — בשכר טובה זו שיעשו עם אחיהם תנתן להם ארץ הגלעד; ואם לא יתאמצו יותר מאחיהם — "ונאחזו". והכי נפרש: דאי לא כתב "בארץ כנען", ה"א שאם לא יעברו חלוצים בראש המלחמה ולא יסייעו בכיבוש הארץ אלא כשאר שבטים, כלל וכלל לא יטלו מארץ כנען; קמשמע לן, דאף על פי כן יטלו. וקשה: דהיכי תיסק אדעתיה שלא יטלו כלל בארץ כנען, כיון שסייעו בכיבוש כמו אחרים?! וי"ל: דסד"א, כיון שהוקצה ארץ כנען לשאר שבטים — שהרי מאותה שעה ששאלו בני גד ובני ראובן ארץ גלעד, נעשו כמו שסלקו עצמן מלחלוק בארץ כנען — ונימא שאם לא יקיימו תנאם לא יהיה להם חלק בה; קא משמע לן "בארץ כנען", לומר שיטלו חלקם כשאר שבטים כאן וכאן. ואם תאמר: לכתוב קרא "בארץ כנען" בלבד, ולא נכתוב "ונאחזו בתוככם", וממילא ידענו: כיון שנוטלים חלקם בארץ שהוקצה לשאר שבטים, כ"ש שיטלו חלקם בארץ גלעד שלא הוקצה לשאר שבטים? וי"ל: דאדרבה, ה"א בארץ כנען שלא נתייפה כחם — דין הוא שיטלו, אבל בארץ גלעד שנתייפה כחם בה — יקנסו ממנה ולא יקחו בה כלל; לכך נכתבו שניהם:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 61b:2:1.english: "If [the Merciful One] had not written: 'In the land of Canaan,' I would say: 'Among you' [means] in the land of Gilead" - [Rashi] explained in the Kuntres: That if they do not cross over, they will take their portion according to what is due to them in the land of Gilead, in which they already took possession, and they helped [you] conquer it; but in the land of Canaan, not at all, as they did not help conquer it. [Therefore, the verse] teaches us that nevertheless, they will take [a portion in the land of Canaan]. And this is difficult: For what logic is there that they should sit in their homes and inherit with their brethren who went out to war?! [And furthermore, it is not similar to the parable that is cited.] Therefore, it appears to the Ri to explain that the plain sense of the verse is as follows: If they cross over armed at the head of the army to be first in battle, as reward for this goodness that they do for their brethren, the land of Gilead will be given to them; but if they do not exert themselves more than their brethren, [then] "they shall receive a possession" [equally with them]. And this is how we explain [the Gemara]: If [the verse] had not written "in the land of Canaan," I would say that if they do not cross over armed at the head of the battle and do not assist in the conquest of the land [any more] than the other tribes, they would not receive [a portion] from the land of Canaan at all. [The verse therefore] teaches us that nevertheless, they will take [their portion in the land of Canaan]. And this is difficult: How could it enter [anyone's] mind that they would not receive [a portion] at all in the land of Canaan, given that they assisted in the conquest like the others?! And one can say: It might enter your mind to say [that] since the land of Canaan was designated for the other tribes — for from the moment the children of Gad and the children of Reuben requested the land of Gilead, they became as though they had removed themselves from dividing the land of Canaan — and we would say that if they do not fulfill their condition, they will have no share in it. [Therefore, the verse] teaches us "in the land of Canaan," to say that they will take their portion like the rest of the tribes, both here and there. And if you say: Let the verse write only "in the land of Canaan" and not write "and they shall receive a possession among you," and we would know on our own: since they take their portion in the land that was designated for the other tribes, all the more so they should take their portion in the land of Gilead, which was not designated for the other tribes?! And one can say: On the contrary, I would say that in the land of Canaan, where their right was not enhanced, it is right that they should take [a portion]; but in the land of Gilead, where their right was enhanced, they should be penalized regarding it and should not take [any portion] in it at all. Therefore, both of them were written.
